_README: FROZEN Lighthouse baseline — the score FLOOR enforced by
Semantics: floors.<slug>.<category> = the MINIMUM score (0-100) that route may
report for that category. The reported score is the MEDIAN of LH_REPEATS passes.
Measured < floor => CI FAILS. A route present in
screenshotMatrix.ts::TARGET_PAGES but absent from `floors` FAILS too — an
unbaselined route is a hole, not a pass.
This is a RATCHET: the floor may only ever RISE. It is today's measured score
with no margin subtracted. Lowering a floor is a deliberate, written trade-off,
never a way to make CI green — the same rule as a11y-baseline.json.
`accessibility` is NOT a category here and never will be. axe-core owns that
question (a11y-baseline.json, per-page per-rule node ceilings, adjudicated in
is evidence for the A-08 screen-reader audit.

provenance.measured_by: GitHub Actions — E2E workflow, job 'Lighthouse — score ratchet vs. the seeded stack (RC P11-8)'
provenance.conditions: seeded Compose stack (SEED_E2E_GOLDEN + SEED_ESP_TA + SEED_RATIONALE), Admin login performed by the spec but NOT carried into the scored tab (measured 2026-08-31 - see session_state_2026_08_31; this clause used to read 'Admin session' and that was counterfactual), 1440x900 desktop form factor, simulated throttling at Lighthouse's own desktop preset (rttMs 40, throughputKbps 10240, cpuSlowdownMultiplier 1), maxWaitForLoad 20000 ms, median of 3 passes per route after a discarded warm-up
provenance.measured_pre_merge: Measured on the P11-8 branch, not on main: the whole point of the run was to record the tree WITH the gate in it. The next main run must reproduce these numbers exactly — if it does not, this file is wrong, not the run.
provenance.stability: The measuring run saw 0 points of spread everywhere. The very next run did NOT: panel-management's performance passes came in 98-100 while its median stayed 98. So 'zero spread' is a property of one run, not of this gate, and it is recorded that way on purpose. What actually holds the floor is the MEDIAN, and it held: both runs reported 98 for that route. If a future run starts flapping, the answer is more repeats or a warm-up change - never a lower floor.
provenance.sensitivity_boundary: performance sits at 100 on 22 of 23 routes. That is a real measurement, not a rounding artefact, and it is also this gate's weakest axis: against a localhost stack on the desktop preset the score is saturated, so only a substantial regression will move it. A floor of 100 means 'may not get worse at all' — the strictest ratchet available — but it is not evidence that the app is fast on a real user's machine. The per-route FCP/LCP/TBT/CLS/SI in lighthouse-report/lighthouse-results.json do differentiate the routes and are reported, never gated.
provenance.do_not_tighten: panel-management/performance must stay at 98. It is the one route with measured repeat variance (98-100 across 3 passes), so a run whose median reads 100 will make the tightened map suggest raising it. Taking that suggestion arms a gate that fails the next time the same route medians at 98 - a flapping gate nobody asked for. Every other floor may be tightened normally when a real improvement lands.
provenance.tightened_2026_08_30: GH #677 / ADIM 145 (PR #884). The `seo` floor was raised 82 -> 100 on all 23 routes after `meta-description` and `robots-txt` were fixed in the SPA shell. Measured by the SAME gate that enforces it: E2E workflow run 33334644272, job 'Lighthouse', LH_REPEATS=3, seeded Compose stack — NOT from a developer machine. An earlier local run was deliberately NOT used: this file's own `sensitivity_boundary` records that the score is comparable only inside its own runner class, so a floor copied off Apple Silicon would arm a gate that fails on the next CI pass. `performance` and `best-practices` floors are UNCHANGED, and panel-management/performance stays at 98 per `do_not_tighten` (that run medianed 98, so the tightened map did not even suggest raising it). Two deductions remain open and are declared in #677: errors-in-console (23/23) and cumulative-layout-shift (panel-management).
provenance.session_state_2026_08_31: ADIM 147. EVERY FLOOR IN THIS FILE WAS MEASURED SIGNED OUT, and until 2026-08-31 nothing said so. The spec logs in with `ensureAdmin(page)`, but that page lives in a Playwright-created browser context while Lighthouse - called with no `page` argument - attaches over the DevTools port and opens its own tab in the DEFAULT context, which has a separate localStorage partition. Measured end to end against the installed packages, not inferred: lighthouse@13.4.1 core/gather/navigation-runner.js:278-282 takes the `puppeteer.connect({browserURL}).newPage()` path; puppeteer-core cdp/Browser.js:204 routes that to `#defaultContext`, constructed at :76 with an id of `undefined`, so :211-213 issues Target.createTarget with NO browserContextId; a tab opened exactly that way reads the session key back as null while the Playwright context still reads the token. `disableStorageReset: true` is necessary but not sufficient - it stops Lighthouse clearing storage it was never going to see. CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS FILE: the floors are NOT wrong, they are floors for a world nobody had named. They remain enforceable and comparable against any other run that also reports `session_carried_into_lighthouse_tab: false` (the spec now measures and reports that per run). THEY MUST NOT BE COMPARED WITH AN AUTHENTICATED RUN. Fixing the harness moves all 23 routes and REQUIRES a full re-freeze from a CI run, per this file's own `sensitivity_boundary` - never from a developer machine. NOT CLAIMED: that the app is free of console errors when signed in. The errors-in-console deduction declared in `tightened_2026_08_30` is a property of the signed-out shell; whether it also holds for the authenticated app is UNMEASURED.
provenance.cls_fixed_2026_08_31: ADIM 148. The cumulative-layout-shift deduction named in `tightened_2026_08_30` is FIXED at its source, so that clause is now correct only as history. panel-management was the ONLY route below performance 100, and its whole deduction was one 25-weight CLS audit; the `layout-shifts` diagnostic named the System actors card sliding down. Cause: each panel card's body renders 166px while its query is in flight and 244px once settled - 78px of growth each, 234px of downward push - so every card shoved the ones beneath it. Fix: .panel-card-async reserves the settled height for the in-flight body (min-height, never height). Measured in a local harness that first reproduced this gate's own numbers (panel-management 0.0898 vs CI 0.085; create-package 0.0361 vs CI 0.035): CLS 0.0898 -> 0.0000516, audit score 0.92 -> 1, while the untouched control route create-package stayed at 0.036. THE FLOOR IS DELIBERATELY NOT TIGHTENED. `do_not_tighten` still governs panel-management/performance and it stays at 98; a run that now medians 100 will make lighthouse-baseline.tightened.json suggest raising it, and that suggestion must still be refused. NOTE THE CONSEQUENCE: with the floor at 98 this gate CANNOT fail if the fix is reverted, so the reservation is pinned by frontend/src/test/panelManagement.test.tsx instead ('reserves each async panel card's height while its query is in flight'), whose negative control failed exactly one test. NOT CLAIMED: that the authenticated route has no layout shift - like every number in this file it was measured against the signed-out shell, which is what this gate scores (measured separately in ADIM 147 / PR #887).
provenance.session_carried_2026_08_31: ADIM 150. THE HARNESS IS FIXED: specs/21-lighthouse.spec.ts now logs in inside the browser's DEFAULT context (chromium.launchPersistentContext), which is the context Lighthouse's own tab opens in, so every route is scored SIGNED IN. The mechanism was measured app-independently against a synthetic origin, driving lighthouse's own puppeteer-core rather than a model of it: with `browser.newContext()` the Playwright page reads the token and the Lighthouse tab reads null; with `launchPersistentContext` both read it. The spec's own probe (chromium.connectOverCDP -> contexts()[0]) was cross-checked against that real puppeteer path and agrees in BOTH worlds, which is why the probe can now be a gate: conditions.session_carried_into_lighthouse_tab must be `true` or the run fails, because a signed-out run is not comparable to the floors below. AS OF THIS COMMIT THE FLOORS ARE STILL THE SIGNED-OUT ONES and are therefore NOT comparable to what this spec now measures -- the first CI run on this branch is EXPECTED to be red. The floors are re-frozen from that run's own lighthouse-report artefact in the next commit, never from a developer machine (sensitivity_boundary), which is the same two-commit shape tightened_2026_08_30 used. Re-freezing across a world change is NOT the forbidden 'lower a floor to make CI green': that rule governs a drop WITHIN one world, while this file's own contract (session_state_2026_08_31, and the conditions clause) already declares floors world-scoped and comparable only against a run in the same world.

policy.accessibility: NOT REQUESTED — axe-core is the shipped a11y authority (frontend/e2e/a11y-baseline.json). Two competing a11y numbers would be two authorities. No Lighthouse output is A-08 evidence.
policy.performance_vs_loadgen: Lighthouse measures the BROWSER (paint, interactivity, layout stability of a route). scripts/loadgen.py measures the SERVER (per-endpoint HTTP p95, control-normalised, nightly ratio gate). docs/performance/README.md section 8 names frontend rendering as out of the load driver's scope; this file covers exactly that declared gap. Neither number may be cited for the other's question.
policy.margin: none — the floor is the measured median, not the median minus a cushion. Noise is answered by repeats + median, never by widening the band.
